content.title: Today’s Wordle #1742 Hints And Answer For Friday, March 27
content.text: How to solve today's Wordle.SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty ImagesTGIF, dearest Wordlers! The weekend is almost here, and then just a couple days later it’ll be April. April Fool’s Day is coming. As if “fake news” wasn’t already a big enough problem! It’s 2XP Friday, so double your points (positive or negative) and best of luck! It’s time to solve this Wordle!Looking for Thursday's Wordle? Check out our guide right here.Today’s Bonus Custom WordleNow that we can create our own custom Wordles, I’m including a bonus Wordle with each daily Wordle guide. These can be 4 to 7 letters long. Hopefully this is a fun extra challenge. Click the link below to play the Wordle I hand-crafted for you.Today’s Bonus Custom Wordle is 7 letters long.MORE FOR YOUThe hint: Nasal defenders.The clue: This Wordle follows a trend from the last two custom Wordles.Yesterday’s Custom Wordle Answer: ACAROIDHow To Solve Today’s WordleHow To Play WordleWordle is a daily word puzzle game where your goal is to guess a hidden five-letter word in six tries or fewer. After each guess, the game gives feedback to help you get closer to the answer: Email Address Green: The letter is in the word and in the correct spot.Yellow: The letter is in the word, but in the wrong spot.Gray: The letter is not in the word at all.Use these clues to narrow down your guesses. Every day brings a new word, and everyone around the world is trying to solve the same puzzle. Some Wordlers also play Competitive Wordle against friends, family, the Wordle Bot or even against me, your humble narrator. See rules for Competitive Wordle toward the end of this post.Today’s Wordle Hints And AnswerWordle Bot’s Starting Word: SLATEMy Starting Word Today: SPIRE (7 words left)The Hint: This material, used in jewelry and other crafts, has been banned across much of the world to protect endangered species.The Clue: This Wordle begins with a vowel.Okay, spoilers below! The answer is coming!...The Answer:Today's WordleScreenshot: Erik KainWordle Bot AnalysisEvery day I check Wordle Bot to help analyze my guessing game. You can check your Wordle score with Wordle Bot right here. SPIRE was a fantastic guess, leaving me with just 7 possible solutions and one yellow and one green box. I came up with a few possible words at this point, and was really debating between INTRO and IVORY. IVORY is just a much nicer word, and I often like to pick my favorite if I can’t decide. I didn’t expect it to be the Wordle! (I checked and Wordle #1049 was EBONY, so now EBONY and IVORY can live in perfect harmony in the Wordle-verse).Competitive Wordle ScoreToday's Wordle BotScreenshot: Erik KainI think I’ve gotten something like three Wordles-in-two this month, which is the only reason I’ve been able to keep pace with the Wordle Bot, who at one point had over a 10-point lead on me. I get 2 points for guessing in two and 1 point for beating the Bot today, which doubles to 6 points for 2XP Friday. The Wordle Bot gets 1 point for guessing in three and loses it for losing to me. I take the lead for the first time in weeks:Erik: 22 pointsWordle Bot: 19 pointsHow To Play Competitive WordleGuessing in 1 is worth 3 points; guessing in 2 is worth 2 points; guessing in 3 is worth 1 point; guessing in 4 is worth 0 points; guessing in 5 is -1 points; guessing in 6 is -2 points and missing the Wordle is -3 points.If you beat your opponent you get 1 point. If you tie, you get 0 points. And if you lose to your opponent, you get -1 point. Add it up to get your score. Keep a daily running score or just play for a new score each day.Fridays are 2XP, meaning you double your points—positive or negative.You can keep a running tally or just play day-by-day. Enjoy!Today’s Wordle EtymologyIvory comes from Old French ivoire, itself from Latin eboreus (meaning "of ivory"), derived from ebur (ivory), which was borrowed from an ancient Semitic or Egyptian root — the Egyptian âb or abu, meaning elephant. The word entered English in the 13th century, carrying its original meaning of the hard white material from elephant tusks.Be sure to follow me for all your daily puzzle-solving guides, TV show and movie reviews and more here on this blog!
